sec.label: A.
sec.title: Studies on DAG
sec.p: LACHESIS [5] is proposed as a new reinforcement learning algorithm to address the job scheduling problem in heterogeneous environments. LACHESIS, which consists of a GNN and a heuristic algorithm, addresses the heterogeneous environment and the reduction of the decision space of neural networks. Another study applies Actor-Critic (AC) Reinforcement Learning (RL) to DAG scheduling [6]. A heuristic algorithm called SAFLA (Slack Aware Frequency Level Allocator) is proposed as a new cooperative scheduling method [28]. The SAFLA algorithm assigns voltage/frequency levels to tasks so that the total energy consumed by the schedule is minimized.

sec.label: B.
sec.title: DAG Scheduling on Clustered Many-Core Processor
sec.p: A RTE (runtime environment) for clustered many-core architectures is proposed [11]. In this study, the target application is a DAG with redundancy. Furthermore, the DAG is composed of two types of nodes: actor nodes that have information about how the data is processed, and data nodes which represent memory requirements. An extended version of HEFT (Heterogeneous Earliest Finish Time) scheduling is proposed as a scheduling method that can be performed on RTE. A scheduling method for DAG with multiple periodic nodes using the clustered many-core processor has been proposed [14]. This study focuses on Kalray MPPA-256 and is an extension of the study [12]. This study makes the assumption that a single node can process multiple cores. In order to avoid communication contention due to NoC, this study proposes the method where 16 Compute Clusters (CCs) in Kalray MPPA-256 are divided into groups for task allocation and priority determination. In this study, tasks with large core requirements are allocated to one group. It states that communication delays occur when different groups are used for communication between tasks. In other words, only inter-cluster communication between nodes is considered. In our study, we consider not only between nodes but also inter-cluster communication occurring within a node. A method of core allocation in MBP (Model-Based Parallelization) for the clustered many-core processor is proposed [19]. This study assumes Kalray MPPA-256 and proposes a cluster selection method that can reduce inter-cluster communication based on path information in the system. However, the number of cores allocated to a single node is one, and therefore the assumption is that inter-cluster communication does not occur within a node. This study proposed a method for allocating cores in the clustered many-core processor [18] to avoid resource interference by optimizing the offline and online phases, respectively.

A DAG scheduling method that takes intra-node parallelism into account for clustered many-core processors is proposed [9]. This method assumes that a node can perform parallel processing on multiple cores. An extension of federated scheduling [29] for the clustered many-core processor is studied [13]. The processor envisaged here is Kalray Coolidge MPPA3-80. This research extends the formula for determining the number of cores for high-load tasks in federated scheduling to take into account the inter-cluster communication time. A method of DAG scheduling for multi/many-core platforms that uses LET-P (Logical Execution Time-Process) [30] to prevent memory contention is proposed [10]. Using LET-P, memory contention-free scheduling is possible but it incurs an associated overhead. A scheduling method using clustered many-core processors for DAG considering intra-node parallelism is proposed in study [8]. This research assumes the use of Kalray Coolidge MPPA3-80, and proposes a method called the reduction-effectiveness method, which determines the appropriate number of nodes required for parallel processing in each node.

sec.label: C.
sec.title: Research on Autonomous Driving Systems and DAG
sec.p: The study [4] models the structure of the Apollo autonomous driving system as a DAG and proposes a scheduling method for it. This study claims to be the first study that introduces the Age of Information (AoI) as an evaluation index for scheduling. AoI is the time difference between the time when the sensor acquires the external situation (data) and the time when the control process is actually carried out using the data. The older the data is (the longer it has been generated), the larger the value of AoI becomes, and the larger the value of AoI is, the longer the time from the situation judgment to the vehicle body control is. For example, even if data is obtained that there are no people at point P at a certain time, people may move to point P over time, and the older the data, the more dangerous the situation may become if it is used with trust. In this study, the periodic scheduling problem is defined as an integer linear programming problem to minimize the AoI, and then an approach is proposed to find the optimal solution using reinforcement learning. The study shows that maximizing the throughput and minimizing the response time can be achieved by minimizing the AoI.

In the study [2], Autoware, an autonomous driving system, is modeled as a DAG, and the approach is proposed for early detection of deadline misses in the middle of the path, in contrast to the problem that deadline misses can only be detected at the end of the end-to-end path in a DAG. The approach is proposed to enable early detection of deadline misses in the middle of the path. The approach initially calculates the start and end times of all jobs. Then, for the data output by each job, the criterion called the data freshness constraint is set, and for the two tasks connected by an edge, two points are checked: (i) whether the output data is ready in time for the start of the subsequent job, and (ii) whether the output data satisfies the data freshness constraint, and a dependency relationship is defined as satisfying these criteria. The dependency relationship is defined as being established when these are satisfied. The laxity of all jobs is then calculated based on the dependencies obtained. If the actual job start time exceeds the laxity statically calculated in this way, the system notifies a deadline miss at this point. However, a problem exists in this study: the execution time of each task is defined in WCET, which makes the determination of a deadline miss pessimistic.

To address this pessimism problem, a new concept of plaxity is proposed [3]. Specifically, the execution time of each job is defined as a probability variable, and the value of laxity used to judge deadline misses is the result of a convolution operation of probabilistic execution times between dependent nodes. This results in multiple values of laxity for a single node, with a probability assigned to each value. Here, the pair of multiple laxity values and probabilities for a single node represents the probability of meeting the deadline when the process is started at that time (laxity).

In other research, the study [24] proposes a new model for heterogeneous platforms, HPC-DAG (Heterogeneous Parallel Condition Directed Acyclic Graph Model). In this study, some features of Autoware are modeled with HPC-DAG. In addition, the study [31] proposes a mechanism to reduce deadline misses by modeling autonomous driving systems with DAG and analyzing their end-to-end paths by dividing them as chains.

sec.label: D.
sec.title: Summary
sec.p: Table 5 summarizes prior studies in three categories: general DAG scheduling, autonomous driving DAG models, and DAG scheduling on clustered many-core processors.

General DAG scheduling studies [5], [6], [28] in Table 5, as introduced in Section V-A, utilize DAG models, but they do not specifically target autonomous driving systems and clustered many-core processors. The studies [2], [3], [4], [24] in Table 5, which were presented in Section V-C, model autonomous driving systems using DAGs but do not address clustered many-core processors. The studies [8], [10], [11], [18] discussed in Section V-B, target clustered many-core processors. Although these studies focus on clustered many-core, their objective is not to reduce inter-cluster communication. Similarly, the studies [13], [14], [19], also introduced in Section V-B, address clustered many-core processors and aim to reduce inter-cluster communication. However, no existing research tackles the reduction of inter-cluster communication both within a node and between nodes. The final row in Table 5 represents the proposed method, which models autonomous driving systems as DAG tasks and targets clustered many-core processors (DAG, MAD, and CM). Our approach aims to reduce inter-cluster communication both within a node and between nodes (RIW and RIB). Furthermore, given that the proposed method is independent of specific cluster structures, it is evaluated across multiple cluster configurations (EMC).

From Table 5, it can be said that this study has an advantage over other studies in that it is able to reduce inter-cluster communication both within a node and between nodes. It can also be seen that there are very few studies of DAG for autonomous driving systems using clustered many-core. This study is the first to evaluate multiple cluster architectures for DAG modeling autonomous driving systems.

sec.label: VI.
sec.title: Conclusion
sec.p: This paper presented a dynamic cluster selection algorithm for general-purpose clustered many-core processors. The proposed method is based on an appropriate combination of functions such as Pred_fit, Greedy_fit, Best_fit, Comb_fit and AIS. The proposed method was found to significantly reduce inter-cluster communication compared to existing methods and cluster selection using these methods alone. The results demonstrated that the proposed method can reduce inter-cluster communication both within a node and between nodes.

It was found that the proposed method gave somewhat poorer results than the other methods, either within a node or between nodes depending on the cluster architectures. However, this is due to the reduction of both inter-cluster communication within a node and between nodes. In fact, the proposed method performed better than the other methods for all cluster architectures in the evaluation of response time considering these two inter-cluster communications. We also found the proposed method to be effective in various cluster architectures and task sets.

For future work, we aim to propose a cluster selection algorithm for DAG that takes into account the trade-off between the generation of memory contention and the reduction of inter-cluster communication. We will also investigate the impact of memory contention as a result of increased cluster partitioning. In addition, the evaluation in this paper utilized a randomly generated DAG modeling an autonomous driving system, but it would be useful to conduct an evaluation using execution times obtained from actual driving data to better verify the practical feasibility of the system. It would also be beneficial to conduct the evaluation on an actual device using an actual clustered many-core processor, such as the MPPA3-80 Coolidge.
